marks.name: Benllech Bay
marks.description: Published SeaAngler fishing mark at Benllech Bay. The publication describes fishing close in and advises care around the higher ledges.
tips: SeaAngler reports that many fish can be taken close in.
SeaAngler advises particular care from the higher ledges.
marks.access: Visit Anglesey reports disabled facilities and access for disabled visitors. Fishing Wales reports fishing from the sand and promenade.

source.reference: Benllech Bay Sea Fishing Mark, published 17 June 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Benllech Beach, approximate beach midpoint

marks.parking: Visit Anglesey confirms parking at Benllech Beach; parking charges may apply.

marks.name: Cemlyn Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler published Cemlyn Beach as an easily accessible Anglesey mark, reporting codling, whiting and pouting and noting that the rocks at the end of the beach can also be worth trying.
tips: SeaAngler reported fish between approximately 30 and 100 yards out.
SeaAngler reported that evening was the better time in that report.
The rocks at the end of the beach were reported as worth trying during the day.
marks.access: National Trust and AccessAble report a step-free entrance from the far end of the car park, but the wider coastal route includes gravel, shingle, uneven ground and gates. The shingle ridge is not suitable for wheelchairs.

source.reference: UK Sea Fishing Catch Reports 5.1.10, Anglesey section
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Cemlyn Beach, approximate beach midpoint
source.access_reference: Visit Anglesey, Countryside and coast at Cemlyn

marks.parking: Bryn Aber car park at Cemlyn. National Trust says the car park is affected by tides and should be checked against tide times.

marks.name: Garth Pier
marks.description: SeaAngler published Garth Pier as a sea-fishing venue, reporting bass to double figures along with cod, pollack, wrasse, mackerel and dogfish. The pier's current official visitor information confirms that fishing is currently permitted with a fishing pass.
marks.access: Fishing is permitted with a fishing pass. Current official information lists £3 for a day fishing pass and £10 annually.

source.reference: Book This Pier for Just a Quid, published 9 September 2009
source.location_reference: Garth Pier coordinates independently checked against published geographic sources

marks.parking: Garth Pier has on-site car parking. The official pier information lists £2 car parking and free parking for Blue Badge holders.

marks.name: Calshot
marks.description: SeaAngler published Calshot as a shallow sea-fishing venue at the mouth of Southampton Water.
tips: SeaAngler reports the venue generally fishes during the last three hours of the flood and first couple of hours of the ebb.
SeaAngler recommends night sessions.
marks.access: The venue includes shingle beaches. Hampshire County Council confirms accessible parking and wheelchair access at the Activities Centre, but this does not establish wheelchair access to the fishing position.

source.reference: Calshot Sea Fishing Mark, published 18 May 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Calshot Beach, approximate beach midpoint
source.current_location_reference: Hampshire County Council Calshot visitor information

marks.parking: Hampshire County Council confirms parking at Calshot Activities Centre; current local parking arrangements should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Sandwich Bay
marks.description: SeaAngler published Sandwich Bay as a sea-fishing mark and identifies the 10th green near the slipway as a popular mark.
tips: SeaAngler reports fishing from low water up to high water can produce catches.
SeaAngler reports coloured water, especially after a south-westerly blow, can be productive.
marks.access: The beachfront includes sandy, unsurfaced paths and sand/shingle. Access conditions vary and some areas are restricted.

source.reference: Sandwich Bay Sea Fishing Mark, published 18 June 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Sandwich Bay, approximate beach midpoint

marks.parking: Sandwich Bay Estate operates paid vehicle access and an unpaved parking area near the beachfront. Charges and access restrictions apply.

marks.name: Blue Anchor
marks.description: SeaAngler published Blue Anchor as a group of shore marks covering the wall beside the road, the beach in front of the chalets and rocky reefs.
tips: SeaAngler reports the wall and beach fish best on tides over five metres, with larger tides more productive.
SeaAngler warns that the tide retreats a long distance at low water and that mud and quicksand are present.
marks.access: The seafront promenade is long and flat, but Blue Anchor beach access includes steep steps that are not suitable for wheelchairs. The published fishing mark also includes rocky reefs, so accessibility to the fishing positions varies.

source.reference: Blue Anchor Sea Fishing Marks, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Blue Anchor Beach, approximate beach midpoint

marks.parking: Somerset Council lists Blue Anchor Car Park as free, long-stay, 24-hour parking with four disabled bays.

marks.name: White Mark & Gasworks
marks.description: SeaAngler published White Mark and Gasworks as fishing marks to the left of Minehead harbour. White Mark is described as a low-water mark, while Gasworks fishes around dead low water.
tips: SeaAngler reports White Mark fishes around two hours either side of low water.
SeaAngler reports the sand is uncovered at dead low water at Gasworks.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to the harbour and promenade, then a footpath through the woods to the beach. The White Mark is to the left and Gasworks is in front of the footpath towards the bay.

source.reference: White Mark & Gasworks sea fishing marks, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: Minehead harbour/promenade access area; coordinates used are for the verified access/parking area, not an exact fishing position

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports pay-and-display parking along the harbour and promenade.

marks.name: Bossington
marks.description: SeaAngler published Bossington as a steep shingle beach fishing mark on the eastern edge of Porlock Bay.
tips: SeaAngler reports daylight bottom fishing can produce after a strong west wind when the water is coloured.
SeaAngler reports night fishing is more productive in clear conditions.
Morning and evening high tides are reported as good times for float fishing and spinning.
marks.access: SeaAngler says the beach is about a 10-minute walk from the Bossington car park along a rough track. It says driving the track is possible but the track is narrow and badly potholed.

source.reference: Bossington Sea Fishing Mark, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: Bossington village/access area; coordinates are for the verified village area, not the exact fishing position

marks.parking: National Trust Bossington car park. National Trust lists accessible parking spaces.
marks.parking_cost: £2 for two hours; £5 all day; free for National Trust members and Blue Badge holders

marks.name: Cheyne Section
marks.description: SeaAngler published Cheyne Section as a rugged flood-tide mark on Portland's eastern flank, with high ledges and a scramble to the water near the old pipe access.
tips: SeaAngler describes Cheyne Section as a flood-tide venue.
SeaAngler says the better ledges are a few hundred yards south of the initial access point.
SeaAngler gives summer and autumn as the season.
marks.access: SeaAngler describes access via a footpath through an old quarry and notes lofty ledges around 40 feet above the sea. A scramble to the water is possible near the old pipe access.

source.reference: Cheyne Section Sea Fishing Mark, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: Cheyne Weares parking/access area; coordinates are for the verified access area, not an exact fishing ledge
source.access_reference: Cheyne Weares car park location independently checked

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports some free parking on the left before the yellow lines near Southwell. A separately checked Cheyne Weares car park is also in the access area.
marks.parking_cost: free roadside parking reported by SeaAngler; other nearby parking may have separate charges

marks.name: Rhos-on-Sea
marks.description: SeaAngler published Rhos-on-Sea as a popular bass mark at the site of an old pier.
tips: SeaAngler recommends a rising tide around dawn or dusk.
SeaAngler reports September and October as the best period for bass.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers along the promenade to Rhos Point and reports ample car parking with a short walk to the beach.

source.reference: Rhos-on-Sea Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports ample car parking along the promenade near Rhos Point.

marks.name: Llandudno Pier
marks.description: SeaAngler published Llandudno Pier as a sea-fishing mark with safe angling areas on the pier.
marks.access: SeaAngler describes safe angling from the pier platform and surrounding railings. Visit Wales lists mobility accessibility facilities at the pier, but this does not by itself verify wheelchair access to fishing positions.

source.reference: Llandudno Pier Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: Seafront/pier parking arrangements apply; current charges should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Llanddulas
marks.description: SeaAngler published Llanddulas as a steep shingle-backed beach mark with deeper water around high tide.
tips: SeaAngler reports the middle flood through high water as the best period.
SeaAngler reports rougher north-west to northerly weather can improve bass and cod fishing.
Longer casts can be important for plaice.
marks.access: SeaAngler says the beach is clearly signposted from the A55 and that car parking is directly above the beach.

source.reference: Llanddulas Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: Car parking directly above the beach, according to SeaAngler.

marks.name: Pendine Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler published Pendine as a classic Welsh storm beach that fishes best after a good onshore blow with reasonable surf and coloured water.
tips: SeaAngler reports flounder from autumn through spring and summer.
SeaAngler reports bass in spring, autumn and early winter.
marks.access: Visit Wales reports parking adjacent to the beach entrance. SeaAngler describes the beach as a classic storm beach.

source.reference: Pendine Beach Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: Parking adjacent to the beach, according to Visit Wales.

marks.name: The Knap
marks.description: SeaAngler published The Knap as a productive shingle beach and specifically describes it as easily accessible and suitable for junior or less-able anglers.
tips: SeaAngler recommends two to three hours over high water on mid-range to spring tides, especially at night.
SeaAngler reports a light to moderate west to south-westerly wind can create productive surf.
marks.access: SeaAngler describes the mark as easily accessible and suitable for junior or less-able anglers. This does not establish wheelchair access to the fishing position.

source.reference: The Knap Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: Parking/access arrangements should be checked locally before travel.

marks.name: Goldcliff Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler published Goldcliff as a Welsh fishing location with fishing from the sea wall on larger tides and from exposed mud and peat beds on smaller tides.
tips: SeaAngler warns that the tide can run very hard and that anglers fishing the mud and peat must avoid being cut off by the incoming tide.
SeaAngler reports night fishing is favoured by local anglers.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to park at the end of the lane behind the sea wall without blocking private drives or access points.

source.reference: Goldcliff Beach Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports free parking at the end of the lane behind the sea wall; do not block private drives or access points.

marks.name: Talacre
marks.description: SeaAngler published Talacre at the mouth of the River Dee, noting both shallow and very deep water and the need to beware of the incoming tide.
tips: SeaAngler reports plaice, silver eels, school bass and flounder from April to June.
SeaAngler reports dab, flounder, whiting and codling from late October to February.
Beware of the incoming tide.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to Talacre village, the dead-end embankment and then a walk back towards the green light. It advises finding a safe place to park.

source.reference: Talacre Sea Fishing Mark, published 2021
source.location_reference: Venue or access-area coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; not an exact fishing position unless explicitly stated

marks.parking: SeaAngler advises finding a safe place to park near the Talacre embankment and not obstructing access.

marks.name: Burrow Head

location.area: Isle of Whithorn, Dumfries and Galloway

marks.description: SeaAngler published Burrow Head as a group of rock marks near Isle of Whithorn, with deeper water off the front point and easier marks to the left.
tips: SeaAngler reports the various rock marks can fish at any state of the tide.
The tidal pull can be severe off the front point.
SeaAngler reports summer is the main season for most species and mackerel can be present to October.
marks.access: Access is via the narrow road from Isle of Whithorn to the caravan and camping site at Burrow Head. Some marks are unsuitable for children; SeaAngler notes easier marks to the left.

source.reference: Burrow Head Sea Fishing Mark, published June 2021
source.location_reference: Published venue location independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are not claimed to be an exact casting position.

marks.parking: Access is through the caravan and camping site; arrangements for visiting anglers should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Saltwick Bay
marks.description: SeaAngler published Saltwick Bay as a versatile Yorkshire coast mark for cod, flounder and coalfish.
tips: SeaAngler lists September to March as the season.
Recommended baits include crab, lugworm and mussels.
marks.access: SeaAngler says the mark is accessed by a road leading to a caravan site, with a walk to the mark. North York Moors National Park notes that the beach can be cut off at high tide.

source.reference: Saltwick Bay Sea Fishing Mark, published June 2021
source.location_reference: Published venue location independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are not claimed to be an exact casting position.

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports parking on the grass verge outside the caravan site. Current restrictions should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Carn Du, Lamorna
marks.description: SeaAngler published Carn Du as the rocky outcrop on the north-east corner of Lamorna Bay, offering deep water at most states of the tide.
tips: SeaAngler recommends the flood tide, with summer high water around 8pm to 10pm.
Night is best for conger eels, bull huss and occasional larger pollack.
The southwest face is unfishable because of The Heaver rock.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to park in the main car park at Lamorna Cove, cross the footbridge and follow the coastal footpath around the northern side of the bay.

source.reference: Carn Du, Lamorna Sea Fishing Mark, published June 2021
source.location_reference: Published venue location independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are not claimed to be an exact casting position.

marks.parking: Main car park at Lamorna Cove.

marks.name: Eype
marks.description: SeaAngler published Eype as a Dorset sea-fishing mark offering a wide variety of species from May through the end of the year.
tips: SeaAngler reports the best action is on a night flood tide, especially after a blow.
The western end is increasingly snaggy and tackle losses are expected.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to Eype via a minor road and reports a small cliff-top car park.

source.reference: Eype fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: Small cliff-top car park.

marks.name: Seatown
marks.description: SeaAngler published Seatown as a Dorset mark between West Bay and Lyme Regis, with a shelving shingle beach and rougher ground farther west.
tips: SeaAngler reports the venue can come alive after a south-westerly blow when the water is coloured.
SeaAngler warns the beach can be dangerous with a big swell.
marks.access: A small stream runs beside the car park and the favoured fishing area is about 300–400 metres to the left under the cliff.

source.reference: Seatown fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: Car park beside the beach.

marks.name: Monmouth Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler published Monmouth Beach as a rough-ground fishing venue at Lyme Regis, with rocky scars extending into Chippel Bay.
tips: SeaAngler reports the venue is worth visiting from mid-April onwards.
As the tide floods, fish move along the edge of rocky shelves and gullies.
marks.access: Monmouth Beach is accessed from Lyme Regis; the fishing ground changes from shingle and sand to rough ground and rocky scars toward low water.

source.reference: Monmouth Beach fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: Local Lyme Regis parking applies; current restrictions and charges should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Weston Shore
marks.description: SeaAngler published Weston Shore as a long shingle beach on Southampton Water giving way to shallow mud and sand.
tips: SeaAngler reports flounder in April and October to January, with summer producing other species.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers via Weston and the A3025. Weston Shore has shingle beach and intertidal mudflat.

source.reference: Weston Shore fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: Parking is available along the Weston Shore area; current local restrictions should be checked.

marks.name: Gypsy Lane, Lepe
marks.description: SeaAngler published Gypsy Lane at Lepe as a shallow mark with a cast reaching deeper water in the Beaulieu River, fishing from July through February.
tips: SeaAngler recommends evening sessions in summer.
SeaAngler reports September can produce summer species and black bream, while flounder become a main daytime target later in the year.
marks.access: SeaAngler describes a quiet venue reached via Gypsy Lane at Lepe.

source.reference: Gypsy Lane, Lepe fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports free parking.

marks.name: Shoreham Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler published Shoreham Beach as a shallow beach where rock groynes provide hotspots.
tips: SeaAngler lists harbour rag, peeler crab, lugworm and ragworm as recommended baits.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to the beach via West Beach Road.

source.reference: Shoreham Beach fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: Car parking behind the beach huts, according to SeaAngler.

marks.name: Rottingdean
marks.description: SeaAngler published Rottingdean as a popular bass mark with convenient beach access beside a public car park.
tips: SeaAngler lists summer for bass and winter for cod.
marks.access: SeaAngler says the beach is conveniently accessible next to the public car park.

source.reference: Rottingdean fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.parking: Public car park behind the White Horse pub, according to SeaAngler.

marks.name: Selsey West Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler identified Selsey, with West Beach the popular area, as a standout venue for smoothhound and tope.
tips: SeaAngler reports evening flood tides in calm weather are considered best.
SeaAngler identifies peeler crab and squid as favourite baits.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to Selsey Bill and describes West Beach as a steep shingle beach with deep water close in.

source.reference: Selsey West Beach fishing mark
source.location_reference: Venue coordinates independently checked against geographic sources; coordinates are approximate venue locations, not claimed to be exact fishing positions.

marks.name: Bridging Camp, Chesil Beach
marks.description: Published SeaAngler fishing mark on the Bridging Camp section of Chesil Beach. The published mark is a stretch of beach rather than a single casting point, so the app deliberately does not assign an invented GPS position.
tips: SeaAngler reports the first two hours of a young flood can produce codling.
SeaAngler reports other species around two hours either side of high water.
SeaAngler warns that a big swell sweeping up the shingle can make the venue dangerous.
marks.access: SeaAngler describes the fishing area as a half-mile hike from Ferry Bridge car park along the shingle. The whole section can produce, so the fishing position is intentionally recorded as an area rather than an exact pin.

source.reference: Bridging Camp, Chesil Beach Sea Fishing Mark, published 17 June 2021
source.location_reference: SeaAngler identifies the Bridging Camp section and describes the route from Ferry Bridge car park; no exact fishing coordinate is being inferred.

marks.parking: Ferry Bridge car park is the access point described by SeaAngler. The fishing mark itself is approximately a half-mile walk along the shingle from the car park.

marks.name: Durdle Door
marks.description: Published SeaAngler shore-fishing venue at Durdle Door. The fishing area is recorded as a named coastal area rather than assigning an exact casting coordinate.
tips: SeaAngler reports a rising tide as productive.
The venue is a shingle beach and access conditions should be checked before setting out.
marks.access: SeaAngler reports parking close to the Lulworth caravan site. The exact fishing position is not assigned a GPS pin.

source.reference: UK sea-fishing catch report covering Durdle Door
source.location_reference: Named Durdle Door/Lulworth coastal area; no exact fishing coordinate inferred.

marks.parking: Parking is reported close to the Lulworth caravan site; current access and charges should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Southsea Castle
marks.description: Established Southsea seafront shore-fishing mark beside Southsea Castle. Current fishing information identifies the public shingle and sand frontage as a shore mark; established Portsmouth fishing guidance also identifies the area as a recognised mark.
tips: Use suitable public beach/seafront frontage rather than castle walls, ramparts or fenced areas.
The seafront can be very busy; quieter periods are more practical.
marks.access: Public Southsea seafront access. The castle is a managed heritage attraction; obey current signs and event restrictions.

source.publication: Where's The Fish?; Total Fishing; Southsea Castle official visitor information

source.location_reference: Southsea Castle location checked against published geographic mapping

marks.parking: Wider Southsea seafront parking; check current charges and restrictions

marks.name: Portchester Castle
marks.description: Recognised Portsmouth Harbour shore-fishing mark at Portchester, with fishing from suitable tidal foreshore and public harbour-edge areas rather than from the historic castle structure itself.
tips: The flood and high-water period is important at this shallow harbour mark.
Do not assume castle grounds or walls are fishing access; use lawful public shoreline and follow site notices.
marks.access: Fishing is associated with the tidal waterfront around Portchester rather than the castle itself. English Heritage confirms the castle is a managed historic site; check fishing permission at the exact shoreline position.

source.publication: Where's The Fish?; Fishmag; English Heritage
source.reference: Independent cross-reference of current fishing information with official/location sources
source.location_reference: English Heritage published latitude/longitude for Portchester Castle access location

marks.parking: Charged parking 200m from castle entrance; waterfront arrangements may differ

marks.name: Round Tower
marks.description: Recognised Old Portsmouth harbour-mouth fishing mark from the public waterfront around the Round Tower, with deep tidal water and strong flow close to the wall.
tips: Fish the public waterfront around the tower, not the historic structure itself.
Keep clear of navigation routes, passing vessels and crowded pedestrian areas.
marks.access: Public Old Portsmouth waterfront around the historic Round Tower. Access can change because of events, works, barriers or harbour-security requirements; fish only where current signage permits.

source.publication: Where's The Fish?; Portsmouth City Council/Visit Portsmouth; Historic England
source.reference: Independent cross-reference of current fishing information with official/location sources
source.location_reference: Historic England published location for The Round Tower

marks.parking: Old Portsmouth controlled parking and nearby public parking

marks.name: Victoria Pier
marks.description: Recognised Old Portsmouth fishing location at Victoria Pier and the adjacent Old Portsmouth Beach. Angling Direct identifies Victoria Pier as a Portsmouth sea-fishing mark, while Portsmouth Museum confirms the present pier remains a popular place for fishing.
tips: Angling Direct reports mackerel and garfish around the run-up to high water and sole as a seasonal target.
Strong harbour currents and passing vessel wash require care.
marks.access: Victoria Pier is a small historic pier at the harbour entrance. Portsmouth Museum confirms fishing remains a popular use of the pier; exact access arrangements should still be checked on arrival.

source.publication: Angling Direct; Portsmouth Museum and Art Gallery; British Beaches
